newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand sauntered to a weaker close on Friday after a second assault on the key 4.60 level was rebuffed by importers keen to buy dollars at their cheapest levels in four weeks.
After trading as low as 4.5860 bid and at a high of 4.6255, the rand settled at 4.6210/6260 against the dollar -- slightly weaker than its 4.6180/6230 close on Thursday.
Dealers said the rand's four-day-long rally looked set to continue at the opening, after New York traders bought the currency down to as low as 4.5770 in after-hours trade on Thursday.
"There was some real interest to buy dollars below the 4.60 level until the importers came in and caught a lot of guys short, which took it right back up again," a trader said.
From its low shortly before 0700 GMT, the rand charted a course up to its weakest level by 0900 GMT, where it ran into profit-taking and some exporter selling, dealers said.
In the afternoon session, it fared no better, hovering around the 4.6150 level before drifting up to its close as banks bought dollars in a bid to square their books ahead of the weekend.
"No-one wanted to go home short at the weekend," a trader said.
The rand managed to gain some ground against sterling, firming to 7.7624/7755 from 7.7800/7930 on Thursday and was barely changed at 0.3248/3253 marks from 0.3247/3251 marks previously.
Dealers said that next week the rand was likely to trade in a 4.60 to 4.65 range while keeping an eye out for the release of key economic data -- trade, gross domestic product and money supply.

A Reuters consensus poll of economists forecast the trade surplus would rise to 900 million rand in October from 670 million rand in September, while gross domestic product growth was forecast at 2.5 percent in the third quarter from 3.5 percent in the second quarter.
Private sector credit extension, which dealers felt would be the most important indicator to watch next week, was expected to rise 18.1 percent year-on-year from 17.94 percent in September.
Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals cited burgeoning credit growth as one of the prime reasons behind his surprise one percentage point interest rate hike on Wednesday to 17 percent.
Bond yields fared no better in what dealers described as listless trade.
"The market has gone a bit weaker but it has been lazy and looking for direction," a trader said. "The main reason for the move has been the rand with a bit of profit-taking not helping."
The key R150 settled at 15.98 percent after closing at 15.945 percent on Thursday..

On the money market, banks quoted their three-month NCD rates unchanged at between 16.95 percent and 17.00 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unmoved at between 16.30 and 16.60 percent.
But liquidity remained tight, with the Reserve Bank indicating the shortage higher at 9.65 billion rand on Thursday from 9.378 billion rand on Wednesday.

The Bond Exchange said foreigners bought a net 156.56 million rand worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 211.98 million rand on Wednesday. Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 42.57 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day -- from 5.9 billion rand on Wednesday.
